goal: Tell apart route distance, elapsed time, average speed, and change in speed.

activities.why: Following a toy car makes route length concrete.
A journey also has a beginning and an end in time.
activities.big_question: Could the same road take different amounts of time?

activities.why: Combining distance with time makes a journey comparison useful.
activities.big_question: What does less time for the same road tell us?

activities.why: Speed invites a new question about changes in velocity.
activities.big_question: Could two cars reach the same speed in different times?

explanation: A car card might say 0–60 in 4 seconds. The 4 seconds are elapsed time: how long the speed change took.
Acceleration means how quickly velocity changes. If two cars make the same 0–60 change, the car with the shorter time has greater average acceleration.
card.question: Car A goes from 0 to 60 in 4 seconds. Car B takes 8 seconds. Which car has greater average acceleration?
choices: They have the same average acceleration
hints: Both cars make the same speed change: 0 to 60 miles per hour.
The same change in less time means greater average acceleration.
card.right_text: Yes. Car A makes the same speed change in less time, so its average acceleration is greater.
card.hints_run_out_text: It is Car A. Both cars go from 0 to 60, but Car A does it in less time.
card.picture_idea: Two cars side by side, each with its 0–60 time.
card.picture_description: Two hypothetical cars both go from 0 to 60 miles per hour. Car A takes 4 seconds and Car B takes 8 seconds.
card.how_youll_know: They can say why Car A wins (same change, less time), not just tap it.
card.sources: NASA Glenn Research Center, Displacement, Velocity, Acceleration: https://www.grc.nasa.gov/WWW/K-12/airplane/disvelac.html
card.avoid: 0–60 shows an average; don't say the car speeds up evenly the whole time.
